title: Brother and sister creatures
last: PERFECT JOY HAS NOTHING TO PROVE.

cards: Laudato si', mi' Signore. Praised be you, my Lord. That's the refrain of a song Francis made in the everyday Italian of his own region; you first heard it on day two hundred sixty-nine.
Tradition says he made it late in life, when he was ill and could hardly see. It's called the Canticle of the Creatures, or the Canticle of Brother Sun, and it does something unusual.
It doesn't just list the sun among God's works. It calls him Brother Sun. Then Sister Moon and the stars.
Brother Wind. Sister Water. Brother Fire.

teach.b: Listen to how he describes them. Sister Water is useful and humble and precious and pure. Brother Fire is beautiful and cheerful, strong, and lights up the night.
Sister Mother Earth feeds us, and brings out fruit and colored flowers and grass. Each gets a small portrait, as if Francis knew them personally.
And the little word in each line, per, can be heard more than one way: praised be you for Brother Sun, or by him, or through him. Readers take it differently, and the song may hold all three.
The Bible already has creation singing.

teach.h: SUN AND MOON, PRAISE YE HIM.
teach.b: Psalm one hundred forty-eight calls on everything to praise: "Praise ye him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars of light." Francis takes one step further and gives them family names.
The Little Flowers has stories to match. Francis preaches to a crowd of birds, telling them to thank God for their feathers and the air, and they stay to listen.
Near the town of Gubbio a wolf has been terrifying the people.
Francis goes out to meet him, calls him Brother Wolf, and makes peace: the wolf stops attacking, and the town agrees to feed him.
Then, tradition says, near the very end Francis added one more verse, for one more relative: Sister Bodily Death, whom no one living can escape. Even she is family.
If the sun, the wolf and even death are your siblings, nothing in the world is just a thing.

how: Christians sing or pray Francis's Canticle of the Creatures, sometimes in hymn versions, and some churches bless animals on or near his feast day.

games.q: what does “brother and sister creatures” mean?
o: the names of Francis's very first companions
a rule that friars must care for farm animals
Francis's way of seeing all creation as one family

p: made peace with the town of Gubbio
the last verse, near the end

s: it names sun, moon and stars, wind, water, fire and earth, and later death.
the Canticle calls death a sister
Sister Bodily Death, whom no one living can escape.
Francis wrote the Canticle in the church's Latin
it's in the everyday Italian of his region: laudato si', mi' Signore.

games.q: you're Francis, near Gubbio. a wolf has been terrifying the town, and the people are afraid to go out. what do you do?
o: help the people hunt the wolf down.
go out to meet him, call him Brother Wolf, and make peace.
tell the town to stay indoors until he leaves.
games.why: in the Little Flowers, Francis makes a pact: the wolf stops attacking, and the town agrees to feed him.

practice: Bring to mind one creature you've met today: a dog, a tree outside the window, the water in your glass, the sun on the floor.

Give it Francis's kind of name, Brother Tree, Sister Water, and notice what it does for you without being asked. Then thank it, silently or out loud; if you pray, you can praise God through it, the way the Canticle does.

wordCard.voice: Brother and sister creatures. Francis's way of seeing sun, water, wolf and even death as family, in one household of praise.

orig.note: Umbrian Italian, not Latin: praised be you, the refrain of the Canticle of the Creatures.

carryVoice: Your line: family of creation. In Francis's song, even the water in your glass is kin. Until tomorrow.
